title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 'équation des lacets' is part of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller circle of ideas. Ĝ is a profinite group; the next page has Ĝ = SL(2,Ẑ)'. Inside it sits a subgroup L_0 attached to the data (ρ,σ). B_{ρ,σ} is a group of automorphisms of Ĝ that stabilises L_0 and contains the inner automorphisms int(l) for l ∈ L_0.

The previous page sets the goal: build a group G_{ρ,σ} such that
- Ĝ maps into it as a normal subgroup,
- B_{ρ,σ} maps into it,
- conjugation by the image of B induces the given action on Ĝ,
- Ĝ and B together generate it.

If Z(Ĝ) were trivial, one could simply take the subgroup of Aut(Ĝ) generated by Ĝ and B. Grothendieck rejects that hypothesis as unreasonable, since it already fails for SL(2,Ẑ)/±1.

On this page he notes that the earlier condition B' ⊃ N_0 (N_0 the centraliser of L_0 in Ĝ) is not the right one: it suffices that B contains int(L_0). The construction runs as follows.
- (14) Form the semidirect product S_0G = B ⋉ Ĝ. Define i: L_0 → S_0G by g ↦ int(g)·g^{-1}.
- Conjugation by i(g) acts trivially on Ĝ, so i(L_0) centralises Ĝ.
- i is B-equivariant: int(u)(i(g)) = int(u(g))·u(g)^{-1} = i(u(g)). Hence i(L_0) is normal in S_0G.
- (15) Set G_{ρ,σ} = S_0G / i(L_0).
- (16) This gives maps Ĝ → G_{ρ,σ} and B ↪ G_{ρ,σ}. B embeds because (b,1) ∈ i(L_0) forces l = 1.
- (17) The square L_0 → Ĝ → G and L_0 → B → G (via l ↦ int(l)) commutes, since int(l) ≡ l modulo i(L_0).
- (18) Ker(Ĝ → G) = L_0 ∩ Z(Ĝ) = Ker(L_0 → B).

In modern terms, (L_0 → B) with the B-action on Ĝ is crossed-module data. G_{ρ,σ} is the standard 'semidirect product modulo the anti-diagonal' (a pushout of groups), giving an extension 1 → Ĝ/(L_0∩Z) → G → B/int(L_0) → 1. The next page applies this to SL(2,Ẑ)' and obtains G_{ρ,σ} ≅ GL(2,Ẑ)', with quotient Γ_{ρ,σ} ≅ Ẑ^*.
errors: In the displayed formula (14) the map reads g ↦ int(g^{-1})·g^{-1} (with a scribbled superscript). Only g ↦ int(g)·g^{-1} centralises Ĝ and is a homomorphism, and that is the form used in the verification line. The '-1' on int is a slip or an abandoned correction.

Implicit hypotheses not stated on this page: L_0 must be B-stable (used in b), and int(L_0) ⊂ B. The latter is the relaxed condition B' ⊃ L_0 he announces. Identifying Ker(L_0 → B) with L_0∩Z(Ĝ) requires B ⊂ Aut(Ĝ), i.e. a faithful action, which holds here.

ideas.what: Building a group generated by Ĝ and an automorphism group B containing int(L_0), as (B ⋉ Ĝ)/{int(l)·l^{-1}}, when Ĝ has non-trivial centre.
ideas.modern_name: Quotient of a semidirect product by the anti-diagonal image of a crossed module (pushout of groups / extension realising a given action)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical group/extension theory (Schreier, Eilenberg–MacLane; J.H.C. Whitehead crossed modules)
ideas.where_published: Similar pushout-of-extension constructions appear in SGA 1 (exposé XIII, fundamental group exact sequences) and in the GT/Longue Marche setting, but not this exact text as far as known.

ideas.what: Computing the kernel of Ĝ → G_{ρ,σ} as L_0 ∩ Z(Ĝ), and checking that B embeds.
ideas.modern_name: Kernel computation for the crossed-module quotient

ideas.what: Weakening the hypothesis from B ⊃ int(N_0) to B ⊃ int(L_0) so as to handle groups with centre, such as SL(2,Ẑ).
ideas.modern_name: Choice of hypotheses in a GT-type construction for GL(2,Ẑ)-like groups

deep.surprise_reason: Correct but standard group-theoretic construction (semidirect product modulo anti-diagonal), serving as a technical step that recovers GL(2,Ẑ)' from SL(2,Ẑ)' in a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type framework. Nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: Line 1–2: 'et [-que-] c condition' should read 'et que la condition B'_{ρ,σ} ⊃ N_0 — il suffirait de B'_{ρ,σ} ⊃ L_0'.
(14) map: the image shows int(g^{±1})·g^{-1} with a scribbled superscript. Mathematically, and in the following verification line, it is g ↦ int(g)·g^{-1}.
(16): the crossed-out first symbol is B_{ρ,σ}, replaced by Ĝ; the first map is Ĝ → G_{ρ,σ} (not necessarily injective), the second B_{ρ,σ} ↪ G_{ρ,σ}.

In the parenthesis after b): 'opérant sur L_0 par restriction (tautol.) de l'op. de B_{ρ,σ} sur Ĝ, et sur S_0G_{ρ,σ} ⊃ B_{ρ,σ} par automorphismes intérieurs'. The '{+tautol.+}' insertion sits above 'Bρ,σ', not after 'restriction'.
